$comment: Foundry-owned append-preserving identity lifecycle operation. Not ASA authority. These records live in the registry's identity-operations journal rather than inside a UAO, because uid is a pure function of resolution_key: two uids can never become one by rewriting, so merge and split can only exist as a mapping layer above the derivation. SUPERSEDE and RETIRE additionally have ASA-governed canonical representations (lifecycle_status plus successor_identity_ref) which a future manufacture may carry; this journal records the governed decision, not a rewrite of any immutable package. ENRICH (2026-09-06, ADR-0007) is a third Foundry-owned mapping: it does not change the uid or its lifecycle, only which semantic variant is the identity's current state, and it is verifiable from package bytes.
title: UAO Foundry Identity Operation

operationId.$comment: Content address over the meaning-bearing projection, so the record is self-verifying and cannot be edited in place.

subjects.$comment: Registered identities the operation acts upon. Every subject must already exist in the registry; an operation may not act on an identity that was never manufactured.

targets.$comment: Resulting identities. Empty for RETIRE, which has no successor by definition.

justification.$comment: Required and non-blank. An identity operation without a stated reason is indistinguishable from a mistake once its author is gone.

authority.$comment: Who decided. The Foundry does not adjudicate authority; it records the claim so an auditor can.

enrichment.$comment: ENRICH only. Declares toVariant (carried by toPackageId's occurrence of the subject) the successor state of fromVariant within the same uid. The registry verifies from package bytes that toVariant restates every assertion of fromVariant verbatim and adds at least one; an operation that fails that check is refused at admission and fails verification thereafter.
